001package dayplanner;
002
003
004import java.util.Scanner;
005import java.io.InputStream;
006
007
008/**
009 * <p>
010 * Console input helper backed by a {@link Scanner}.
011 * </p>
012 * <p>
013 * Read methods display prompts and generally retry invalid input. The stream
014 * constructor also supports scripted input, such as a
015 * {@code ByteArrayInputStream} in a small example program, which is actually
016 * used in {@link dayplanner.Tester} for scripted input.
017 * </p>
018 * <p>
019 * The goal of this class is to make user input as easy as possible to deal with
020 * in application classes. So, this class does a lot of the heavy lifting for
021 * you.
022 * </p>
023 */
024public class Input {
025    private final Scanner SCANNER;
026
027
028    /**
029     * Constructs an <code>Input</code> instance that reads from the specified
030     * stream.
031     * 
032     * @param stream Source of input.
033     */
034    public Input(InputStream stream) {
035        SCANNER = new Scanner(stream);
036    }
037
038    /**
039     * Constructs an <code>Input</code> instance that reads from standard input
040     * (<code>System.in</code>).
041     */
042    public Input() {
043        this(System.in);
044    }
045
046
047
048    /**
049     * Reads and returns an integer from user input, prompting repeatedly until
050     * valid.
051     * 
052     * @return The next parseable integer. Invalid lines are rejected and requested
053     *         again.
054     */
055    public int readInt() {
056        int input = 0;
057
058        do {
059            System.out.print("(integer) > ");
060
061            String line = null;
062            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
063                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
064
065            try {
066                if (line == null || line.isEmpty())
067                    throw new NumberFormatException("Empty input");
068                input = Integer.parseInt(line);
069                break;
070            } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
071                System.out.println("\nInvalid integer. Try again:");
072            }
073        } while (true);
074        
075        System.out.print("\n");
076        return input;
077    }
078
079
080    
081    /**
082     * Reads and returns a trimmed string from user input.
083     * 
084     * @return User input as a <code>String</code>, or <code>null</code> if end of
085     *         input.
086     */
087    public String readString() {
088        System.out.print("(string) > ");
089
090        String input = null;
091        if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
092            input = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
093        
094        System.out.print("\n");
095        return input;
096    }
097
098
099
100    /**
101     * <p>
102     * Reads and returns a boolean from user input, prompting repeatedly until
103     * valid.
104     * </p>
105     * <p>
106     * Accepts responses beginning with {@code Y}/{@code y} or {@code N}/{@code n};
107     * characters after the first non-space character do not affect the answer.
108     * </p>
109     * 
110     * @return User input as a boolean.
111     */
112    public boolean readBool() {
113        char input;
114        boolean ret;
115
116        do {
117            System.out.print("(Y/N) > ");
118            
119            String line = null;
120            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
121                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
122
123            try {
124                if (line == null || line.isEmpty())
125                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Input cannot be empty. Try typing Yes or No.");
126
127                input = Character.toUpperCase(line.charAt(0));
128                if (input == 'Y') {
129                    ret = true;
130                    break;
131                } else if (input == 'N') {
132                    ret = false;
133                    break;
134                } else {
135                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid boolean. Try again; try typing Yes or No.");
136                }
137            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
138                System.out.println("\n" + e.getMessage());
139            }
140        } while (true);
141        
142        System.out.println(" ");
143        return ret;
144    }
145
146
147
148    /**
149     * Parses a string representation of time in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format.
150     * 
151     * @param str The string representing a time in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format.
152     * @return A valid {@link Time}, or {@code null} for empty or invalid input. For
153     *         example, {@code 2026/09/15 14:30} produces a time value.
154     */
155    public static Time parseTime(String str) {
156        if (str == null || str.trim().isEmpty())
157            return null;
158
159        String[] components = str.trim().split("[/:,\\s]+");
160        if (components.length < 5)
161            return null;
162
163        try {
164            int y = Integer.parseInt(components[0]);
165            int m = Integer.parseInt(components[1]);
166            int d = Integer.parseInt(components[2]);
167            int h = Integer.parseInt(components[3]);
168            int min = Integer.parseInt(components[4]);
169
170            return new Time(y, m, d, h, min);
171        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
172            return null;
173        }
174    }
175
176    /**
177     * Reads and returns a valid <code>Time</code> from user input, prompting
178     * repeatedly until valid.
179     * 
180     * @return A valid {@link Time}; malformed values are explained and requested
181     *         again.
182     */
183    public Time readTime() {
184        do {
185            System.out.print("(YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM) > ");
186            String line = null;
187            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
188                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
189
190            if (line == null || line.isEmpty()) {
191                System.out.println("\nTime cannot be empty. Please enter format YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM (e.g. 2026/9/10 17:30). Try again:");
192                continue;
193            }
194
195            // Detailed validation error feedback
196            String[] components = line.split("[/:,\\s]+");
197            if (components.length < 5) {
198                System.out.println("\nInvalid format. Expected: YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM (e.g. 2026/9/10 17:30). Try again:");
199                continue;
200            }
201
202            try {
203                int y = Integer.parseInt(components[0]);
204                int m = Integer.parseInt(components[1]);
205                int d = Integer.parseInt(components[2]);
206                int h = Integer.parseInt(components[3]);
207                int min = Integer.parseInt(components[4]);
208
209                Time parsed = new Time(y, m, d, h, min);
210                System.out.print("\n");
211                return parsed;
212            } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
213                System.out.println("\nTime components must be integers. Try again:");
214            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
215                System.out.println("\nInvalid time: " + e.getMessage() + " Try again:");
216            }
217        } while (true);
218    }
219
220    /**
221     * Reads and returns a command string from user input.
222     * 
223     * @return The next line with leading and trailing whitespace removed.
224     */
225    public String readCommand() {
226        System.out.print("(command) > ");
227
228        String input = null;
229        if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
230            input = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
231
232        System.out.print("\n");
233        return input;
234    }
235
236    /**
237     * Prompts the user to press Enter and halts until input is received.
238     */
239    public void pressEnterToContinue() {
240        System.out.println("\nPress enter to continue.");
241        SCANNER.nextLine();
242    }
243}
